One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site.
US President Donald Trump said Monday that he would double tariffs on Canadian vehicles beginning in 2027, as the neighbouring countries spiral towards an escalating trade war.
"On January First, 2027, Tariffs on all Cars, Trucks, both large and small, Automotive Parts, and Steel, will be increased to 50%," he wrote on his Truth Social platform.
The current US tariff on autos stands at 25% for non-US content, while imported steel to the United States generally faces a 50% duty.
Trump's latest threat comes after the North American neighbours failed Friday to reach a deal to avert new 50% tariffs imposed by the Trump administration on select Canadian goods.
Read moreTrump says Canada wants 'benefits of being a State, without being one' as trade war deepens
The White House had alleged "discriminatory treatment" by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products in rolling out the duties.
Trump delayed their implementation by three days last week as Washington and Ottawa stepped up negotiations towards a trade pact.
However, the steep duties took effect Saturday as both sides failed to reach an agreement, and it hits about 5.5% of Canadian goods entering the United States, or some $20 billion worth of products ranging from hockey sticks to cement.
Carney slams 'economic integration as a weapon'
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has since announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States after walking away from what he called a "bad deal."
Read moreCanada vows to match US tariffs 'dollar for dollar' after failed trade negotiations
Carney accused Washington of using “economic integration as a weapon” and said “its signature was written in pencil”. Resorting to the language of battle, he said his country had been “attacked” by the new American tariffs. “You’re at war when you get attacked,” he said, adding that Canada had the reserves, resilience and plan to respond.
But to Trump’s chief trade negotiator, Jamieson Greer, the US was compelled to act after a year of retaliation by its longtime partner.
“We’ve said enough, and so we’ve taken countermeasures. Our interest is in protecting American workers and protecting American supply chains,” the US trade representative told “Fox & Friends Weekend”.
Carney said Canada had been willing to drop remaining retaliatory tariffs on steel, aluminum and autos if the US substantially lowered its own, and to encourage provinces to restore US alcohol sales. But he said Washington’s final demands went too far. “They asked too much and offered too little,” Carney said.
Greer said the Republican administration was offering to cut tariffs on steel, autos and lumber, “things that are sensitive for them. And they’ve always had the best deal, and they still would have an even better deal, but they didn’t want that.”
As a result, he said, “We’re moving forward with measures that respond to Canadian retaliation.”
Carney said the US added last-minute terms that would have reduced tariff relief for Canadian-made vehicles, restricted Canada’s ability to strike trade deals with other countries and weakened protections for language, culture and sovereignty.
He said such demands were “unacceptable”.
The breakdown in negotiations marked a sharp reversal from two days earlier, when officials from the two countries sounded as if they were headed toward a compromise.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford, who leads Canada’s most populous province, praised Carney for rejecting the deal, saying it would have hurt Ontario’s auto, steel and manufacturing sectors. Ford urged Canada to use “every tool in our toolbox” to fight the US tariffs.
The moves also call into question the future of a North American trade agreement covering the United States, Canada and Mexico that is crucial to industry in all three countries.
Carney said the breakdown was “certainly not good news” for the review of that agreement and that the failed negotiations had given Canada “a new perspective” on what Washington wants from the broader economic relationship.
The political impact will likely be even bigger than the economic fallout. The countries sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year.
The US and Canada have wrangled for decades over trade, poking each other over sore spots such as Canadian softwood lumber imports and U.S. access to Canada’s protected dairy market.
Somehow, they still managed to remain friends, allies and trading partners. Canadian soldiers fought alongside Americans in Afghanistan after 9/11. The 5,525-mile US-Canada border is undefended, and nearly 330,000 people and $2 billion worth of goods cross it every day; 800,000 Canadians live in the United States.
Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has imposed tariffs on Canadian goods in a push to bring manufacturing back to the United States and made inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.
Watch moreTrump says Canadians 'want' to become the 51st US state. Is this even possible?
Carney said Canada had recognised that “America has changed” and that the two countries would “not return to our old relationship”.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP and AP)

articles.title: Drone strikes apartment in Kherson, injuring people; woman killed in shelling in region
articles.body:
Drone strikes apartment in Kherson, injuring people; woman killed in shelling in region
According to Ukrinform, the Kherson Regional Prosecutor’s Office reported this.
“According to the investigation, on August 24, 2026, at approximately 12:40 p.m., Russian military forces carried out an attack on Kherson, dropping explosives from an unmanned aerial vehicle,” the statement reads. As noted, an 11-year-old boy who was inside a house at the time of the strike was injured as a result of the attack. The victim was hospitalized. Under the procedural supervision of the Kherson District Prosecutor’s Office, a pretrial investigation has been launched into the commission of a war crime.
According to the Regional Military Administration, the boy sustained blast injuries and an acute stress reaction as a result of the Russian drone attack on the Dniprovskyi District of Kherson.
According to the Regional Military Administration, Russian invaders continue to strike residential buildings in Kherson with drones. During the day, in the city’s Central District, an enemy UAV struck a high-rise apartment building directly. Inside the apartment, the balcony was shattered, windows were blown out, and the walls and rooms were riddled with damage. A 63-year-old man and a 56-year-old woman were injured in the strike. They were diagnosed with blast injuries, closed head injuries, and concussions. The victims are currently under medical supervision. The Regional Military Administration has released a video showing the aftermath of this attack.
In addition, according to the Kherson Regional Military Administration, Russian terrorists killed another resident of the Kherson region—this morning, the occupiers shelled Shyroka Balka in the Stanislav community. A 76-year-old woman sustained fatal injuries as a result of the Russian attack. According to the Regional Military Administration, at around 10:30 a.m., the Russians fired artillery at the village of Komyshany. Three people were injured as a result of the shelling. The 76-year-old woman sustained blast injuries, a closed head injury, a concussion, and a brain contusion. Medical personnel are conducting further examinations and providing her with care. The other two victims—a 75-year-old man and a 28-year-old woman—have been prescribed outpatient treatment.
A 60-year-old resident of Bilozerka, who was caught in Russian shelling of the village that morning, sought treatment at the hospital. He sustained an explosive-blast injury, a concussion, and shrapnel wounds to his torso, arms, and legs. The victim was admitted to the hospital.
It was also reported that in the Korabelny district of Kherson, Russian occupiers killed a man—on the morning of August 23, a middle-aged resident of Kherson sustained fatal injuries as a result of enemy shelling. Relevant authorities are currently working to identify the deceased.
The number of wounded civilians has also been rising in recent days. In particular, two residents of Komyshany required medical assistance after being injured during Russian shelling of the village on August 22. A 70-year-old man and a 69-year-old woman sustained blast injuries, concussions, and acute stress reactions. Both victims will receive outpatient treatment. Another resident of Komyshany, who was attacked by the Russians with a UAV on the night of August 22, sought medical attention at the hospital. As a result of the drone striking his house, the 70-year-old man sustained blast injuries and a concussion. The victim was prescribed outpatient treatment.
A 54-year-old woman from Komyshany, who was caught in the Russian shelling of the village on August 19, also sought medical help. She was diagnosed with blast injury and concussion.
Medical assistance was also provided to two residents of Kherson who were injured the previous morning as a result of a Russian drone attack on the city’s Dniprovskyi district. A 53-year-old man and woman sustained blast injuries, concussions, and acute stress reactions.
As reported by Ukrinform, seven people were wounded in the Kherson region over the past day as a result of Russian strikes.

articles.title: Finland, Ukraine to expand drone cooperation, President says
articles.body:
Şeyma Erkul Dayanç
24 August 2026•Update: 24 August 2026
Finland and Ukraine are expected to reach an agreement on drone cooperation soon, with Finland planning to send 90% of its drone production to Ukraine, Finnish President Alexander Stubb said Monday.
“I think 90% of [Finland's] drone production will go to Ukraine, while 10% of production will remain in Finland,” Stubb said alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a visit to mark Ukraine's Independence Day.
Stubb said the planned agreement would strengthen defense cooperation between the two countries.
He described the planned cooperation as mutually beneficial and compared it with Denmark's model of directly financing Ukrainian defense industry firms.
Stubb said defense cooperation between Finland and Ukraine covers five areas: maritime, air, land, cyber and space.
His delegation to Kyiv included representatives of seven Finnish defense companies. Patria, Insta and Boomeranger signed memorandums of understanding with Ukrainian companies on joint production.
Stubb said international support for Ukraine remained strong and expressed confidence that Ukraine would ultimately prevail in its war with Russia.
The Ukrainian capital is hosting a Coalition of the Willing meeting, bringing together countries supporting Ukraine, including the UK and France.

articles.title: Iran-Cuba economic ties: Unlocking investment potential amid sanctions, legal reform
articles.body:
Iran-Cuba economic ties: Unlocking investment potential amid sanctions, legal reform
TEHRAN- On a global stage increasingly defined by economic fragmentation and unilateral sanctions, two nations with decades of experience in navigating external pressures—Iran and Cuba—are actively seeking to deepen their bilateral economic ties. Recent high-level exchanges and business delegations signal a mutual determination to translate longstanding political solidarity into tangible commercial partnerships.
At the heart of these efforts lies a complex interplay of opportunity and obstacle: Cuba’s gradual opening to private sector participation, Iran’s resilient industrial base, and the persistent logistical and financial barriers that have thus far constrained substantive cooperation.
This report synthesizes the outcomes of two key diplomatic and business engagements—a meeting in Tehran between the Head of the Iran Chamber of Commerce and the Cuban Ambassador, and a subsequent Iranian business delegation visit to Havana in late 2025. While the first part details bilateral discussions on frameworks and aspirations, the second part captures the delegation’s on-the-ground exploration of specific investment projects. Together, they paint a comprehensive picture of a partnership poised for growth, provided that regulatory transparency and payment mechanisms are adequately addressed.
Strategic dialogue in Tehran; laying the groundwork for cooperation
In a significant diplomatic exchange, Samad Hassanzadeh, Head of the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines, and Agriculture (ICCIMA), met with Jorge F. Lefebre Nicolás, the Cuban Ambassador in Tehran, at the place of ICCIMA on August 24, to assess the evolving landscape of Iran-Cuba economic relations. The meeting underscored a shared recognition that while political ties are robust, economic interaction remains below its potential, primarily due to logistical and monetary transfer challenges.
Hassanzadeh opened the dialogue by affirming Iran’s readiness to enter the Cuban market, contingent upon the resolution of two critical bottlenecks: transportation and financial settlements. He stated unequivocally that “if logistical and monetary transfer issues are resolved, Iranian investors will enter the Cuban market.” He identified several promising sectors for joint cooperation, including offshore farming, sugar production, automotive parts, and sanitary products. These areas, he noted, align with Iran’s industrial strengths and Cuba’s import substitution needs.
The Cuban Ambassador responded by detailing the significant legal and structural reforms underway in Cuba. He explained that intensified U.S. sanctions have compelled the Cuban government to overhaul its economic model, pivoting toward a more robust private sector. This shift, he emphasized, has now gained legal status, permitting private banks, exchange houses, and a broader role for foreign investment in previously state-dominated sectors. Ambassador Nicolás invited Iranian investors to consider opportunities in fuel supply and distribution—now managed by Cuba’s private sector—as well as hospitality, where Spanish companies once held sway, and agriculture, where Vietnam has already pioneered land-lease arrangements. He also highlighted mining (nickel and quartz), car rental services, and renewable energy as areas ripe for Iranian participation.
Legal reforms and the private sector as a catalyst
A central theme of the Tehran meeting was the changing legal framework in Cuba. Hassanzadeh stressed the need for written documentation of these new laws to enable the Iran Chamber of Commerce to disseminate accurate information to its members. He recalled previous negotiations with Cuban officials during his visit to Cuba, where proposals for specialized committees to address trade barriers were discussed but not yet implemented. He urged the Cuban side to provide formal investment packages and clear regulatory guidelines, noting that Iranians, having navigated forty years of sanctions-induced restrictions, are uniquely equipped to operate under constrained conditions. He framed economic engagement not merely as a profit-seeking venture but as a religious and moral duty to stand alongside other nations, improving living standards through mutual cooperation.
Ambassador Nicolás acknowledged that transportation remains the primary operational hurdle, yet he expressed confidence that solutions exist, including route reconfiguration and alternative payment corridors that avoid the dollar-based system. He proposed practical next steps: holding online B2B meetings through the embassy, organizing a delegation of interested Iranian companies to visit Cuba, and facilitating a reciprocal Cuban business mission to Iran. He stressed that Iranian companies unafraid of sanctions can operate in Cuba using any currency, and that the Cuban embassy stands ready to act as a bridge for market familiarization.
Sectoral opportunities and the call for concrete action
Hassanzadeh provided additional granularity on potential cooperation areas. He reported on his visits to Cuban farms and sugar production facilities, concluding that joint investment in sugarcane cultivation and sugar processing holds considerable promise. He also floated the idea of designating free trade zones in Cuba exclusively for Iranian products, which would serve as a distribution hub for the Caribbean and Latin American markets. Furthermore, he revealed that official invitations have been extended to Cuba’s Economy Minister, Industry Minister, and Chamber of Commerce President to visit Iran, hoping that such a high-level visit would expedite mutual understanding and deal-making.
The Cuban Ambassador reinforced these overtures by reiterating that Cuba’s new legal framework allows foreign investors to repatriate earnings, a critical assurance for any potential investor. He noted that even the supply and distribution of fuel—a strategic sector—has been privatized, demonstrating the depth of Cuba’s commitment to economic transformation. He concluded by underscoring that this is a favorable moment for Iranian companies, especially large chain enterprises, to enter the Cuban market, provided they move swiftly to understand the new investment laws.
Havana business delegation; from dialogue to due diligence
Moving from high-level political discourse to operational engagement, an Iranian business delegation led by ICCIMA Head Samad Hassanzadeh visited Havana in late November 2025 to explore concrete investment projects aimed at reviving Cuba's idle industrial capacity.
The delegation’s agenda was far more specific than the Tehran discussions, focusing on rehabilitiating dormant factories and establishing joint ventures in sectors where Iran possesses proven technical expertise. In meetings with Cuban officials, Hassanzadeh requested a comprehensive list of non-operational plants, particularly in sugar and cement, to guide Iranian companies seeking investment opportunities. He argued that Iran could play a pivotal role in restoring Cuba’s once-prominent sugar industry, leveraging Iranian machinery and agricultural technology. Similarly, he noted that joint cement production would be more cost-effective than continued imports, and Iranian investors were prepared to construct several cement plants, provided clear regulatory conditions and investment guarantees are established.
Industrial revival and mining as a long-term pillar
ICCIMA Deputy Head Ghadir Ghiyafeh expanded on the industrial front, describing mining as a cornerstone for enduring cooperation. He characterized Cuba as a resource-rich but underdeveloped mining market, where Iranian firms—with advanced technical expertise in mineral exploration, extraction, and processing—could contribute significantly. He specifically mentioned cobalt and nickel production, from geological surveys to processing, and noted that Iranian engineering companies are ready to assist in training Cuban specialists for a planned national steel plant. Khuzestan Steel Company has already signaled its readiness to collaborate. Ghiyafeh projected that a clear legal framework could help push bilateral trade volumes to one billion dollars within five years, targeting construction, roadbuilding, food industries, agriculture, and mining as preferred sectors for Iranian investors.
In a separate meeting with Cuba’s Minister of Domestic Trade, Hassanzadeh urged the preparation of a formal investment package tailored for Iranian companies. He reiterated Iran’s industrial depth across agriculture, mining, petrochemicals, tourism, and energy, but emphasized the necessity of transparent rules and investment security. The Cuban minister responded positively, stating that President Miguel Díaz-Canel had ordered ministries to identify opportunities for importing food, clothing, and consumer goods from Iran, following the 2025 Havana International Fair (FIHAV). The minister stressed that Cuba aims to boost domestic production as a buffer against U.S. sanctions and is prepared to support foreign investors willing to assume risk.
High-level endorsement and the way forward
The visit culminated in a symbolic yet significant moment during Iran National Day at FIHAV 2025. Hassanzadeh declared that the presence of Iranian manufacturers reflected a shared commitment to expanding cooperation, urging both countries to translate political ties into economic outcomes. He outlined additional areas for Iranian contribution, including dam construction, road and housing projects, hydropower development, and renewable energy. Cuba’s Industry Minister, Eloy Álvarez Martínez, echoed this sentiment, calling for practical cooperation to match political solidarity, citing the 2023 comprehensive cooperation agreement as an essential framework for small, medium, and large firms to form direct partnerships.
Most notably, President Miguel Díaz-Canel personally visited Iran’s pavilion at the fair, where he was received by Hassanzadeh, Ghiyafeh, and Iran’s Ambassador to Cuba, Zabihollah Naderi. The Cuban president engaged with representatives of Iranian companies, learning about their products and export capacities. He expressed hope that the exhibition would pave the way for enhanced mutual cooperation and emphasized that his government supports the expansion of economic exchanges and joint investments. His visit underscored the political will at the highest level to pursue tangible results, particularly in petrochemicals, food industries, industrial equipment, and commercial services.
A partnership at a crossroads
The convergence of diplomatic dialogue and business delegation activity reveals a clear trajectory: Iran and Cuba are not merely maintaining symbolic solidarity but are actively engineering a practical economic partnership. The Tehran meeting established the foundational principles—acknowledging legal changes, identifying sectoral opportunities, and agreeing on the necessity of resolving logistical and monetary hurdles. The Havana delegation then tested these principles against reality, identifying specific factories for rehabilitation, mining projects for development, and trade volumes to target.
Three critical takeaways emerge for both sides. First, the resolution of banking and transportation challenges is not just a technicality but the key that unlocks all other potential. Alternative payment mechanisms and shipping routes must be operationalized swiftly. Second, Cuba’s legal reforms must be translated into accessible, written investment guidelines that provide Iranian companies with the confidence to commit capital. Third, the high-level political endorsement, epitomized by President Díaz-Canel’s visit to Iran’s pavilion, must now be followed by bureaucratic efficiency—streamlined permits, clear repatriation rules, and responsive ministerial coordination.
If these conditions are met, the current phase of exploration can transition into a phase of execution. Iran’s industrial resilience, honed under forty years of sanctions, offers a natural complement to Cuba’s resource wealth and strategic location. Together, they have the potential to build a resilient economic corridor that defies external pressures and delivers tangible benefits—in sugar, cement, mining, pharmaceuticals, and beyond—for both nations. The path is clear; the time for decisive action is now.

articles.title: Former US envoy on Ukraine Kellog calls for mobilization of women in Ukraine
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 24. /TASS/. Former US president’s special envoy on Ukraine, Keith Kellogg, has spoken out in favor of mobilizing women to serve with the armed forces of Ukraine.
"My daughter was a soldier. She graduated from the US Military Academy and fought in Afghanistan. Do I believe that women should be mobilized into the army? My answer is yes. Because they fight no worse than men," he told Ukraine’s Naspravdi YouTube channel.
"It is very important that women, as part of society, on into service. On both a personal and professional level, I don’t see a problem," Kellogg added.
General mobilization was declared in Ukraine in February 2022 and has been repeatedly extended. Initially, men aged 27 to 60 were subject to conscription, but the mobilization age was lowered to 25 in April 2024. A law tightening mobilization took effect in the country on May 18 of the same year. Men have tried various ways to avoid conscription or leave the country, often risking their lives. Military enlistment office personnel regularly conduct raids and use force against civilians. But even these measures have failed to address the Ukrainian forces’ personnel shortage. Cases of desertion and unauthorized absence from military units continue to rise. The topics of mobilizing women and lowering the mobilization age further are periodically raised in the country.

articles.title: Russian expert points at lack of substantive agenda for Witkoff, Kushner’s visit
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 24. /TASS/. A visit to Russia by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner is being postponed due to a lack of substantive agenda, Director General of the Russian International Affairs Council Ivan Timofeyev told TASS in an interview.
He recalled Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s remarks that President Vladimir Putin was ready to once again meet with Witkoff and Kushner, but "it’s a question of what they will bring."
"Any consultations and negotiations are based on a specific agenda and require at least a theoretical prospect of reaching a solution, some kind of an algorithm."
"Along with negotiations, any settlement process involves de-escalation measures. But this is quite the opposite of what we are seeing now, as Ukraine has intensified its strikes and Russia has responded," the expert continued. "Western media portrayed these strikes as some sort of a game changer, which is supposed to force Russia to make concessions. As you can see, this did not happen. I don’t think that this kind of escalation will contribute to any sort of settlement."
"The fact that Russian-US consultations and opinion exchanges are ongoing is a good thing, but, so far, I don’t see them yielding any practical results," Timofeyev added.
A source earlier told TASS that the visit to Russia by Witkoff and Kushner is being delayed, and "there are reasons to postpone it.".

articles.title: Across China: Brazilian programmers infuse passion into Chinese humanoid robots
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- A group of Chinese-made humanoid robots competing for the ball on a soccer field immediately came to a halt when commanded to do so by 21-year-old Brazilian programmer Isabela Moura.
Moments earlier, the robots had been positioning themselves, tracking the ball and kicking autonomously, powered by algorithms developed by young Brazilian programmers and researchers.
For Moura, seeing her work drive Chinese humanoid robots on an international stage is both a validation of her programming skills and a reflection of her passion for robotics.
Moura is a member of Team Brazil, formed this year by young researchers from five Brazilian universities to compete in 5-on-5 humanoid robot soccer at the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games (WHRG) in Beijing, which brings together 666 teams from 16 countries.
Hailing from Pernambuco in northeastern Brazil, Moura said her passion for humanoid robots was ignited when she joined RoboCIn, a robotics team at the Federal University of Pernambuco, about 18 months ago. In July, she made her first trip abroad to compete at RoboCup in the Republic of Korea before traveling to Beijing.
"It's a really great experience," she said, adding that the robots used by her team are made by Chinese company Booster Robotics, allowing the Brazilian participants to concentrate on software, artificial intelligence and game strategy rather than building a robot from scratch.
"Developing a robot from scratch would require a lot of time devoted to hardware, communications and embedded systems," Moura said. "With a ready-made Chinese platform, we can focus more on what we do best."
This division of work has given the Brazilian team an opportunity to see its algorithms tested on a real-world robotic platform.
"Seeing what we have developed over the past year actually working is extremely rewarding," Moura said.
The effect is also being felt back at the universities in Brazil. When the Chinese robots operate in laboratories, other students often stop to watch, take photos and record videos. Some have become interested in robotics as a result, Moura noted.
For Team Brazil, however, the competition means more than winning games.
"There is competition here, but competition is not the only reason we came," said Joao Aguiar, a member of Team Brazil and a graduate of FEI University Center, who also participated in the competition last year.
The Brazilian team recently played a friendly match against an Italian team. After the game, members of the two teams discussed different approaches to kicking and positioning robots on the field.
"We talk about what each team does differently," Aguiar said. "Through this kind of exchange, all the teams can improve."
With the Chinese teams, the exchange has developed into technical cooperation. A team from Tsinghua University participated in developing part of Team Brazil's code, while China Agricultural University provided support in areas including game strategy.
Cooperation has continued beyond the competition. "We stay in touch, exchange ideas about what we are working on and also discuss maintenance issues," Aguiar said, recalling the relationship he established with Chinese teams during his first visit to Beijing last year.
His experience in China has also deepened his understanding of the country's humanoid robotics industry. During his first trip to China, Aguiar had the opportunity to closely observe humanoid robots developed by Chinese teams.
"The level of development over the past three or four years has been impressive. You can see how robust, fast and intelligent these robots have become in different scenarios, like logistics, industry and pharmacies," he said.
According to Aguiar, Beijing brings together Chinese and international teams in venues where they can develop, train and test robots while exchanging experience and comparing technical solutions. The competition therefore serves not only as a sporting event, but also as a platform for research, development and international exchange.
Beijing, in addition, is strengthening the infrastructure supporting humanoid robotics. The city announced plans to build a training and evaluation base for humanoid robots this year, said Liu Wenqiang, Party secretary of the China Center for Information Industry Development, at a WHRG press conference.
"Beijing has become a hub for humanoid robotics over the past two years," Aguiar said.
For Flavio Tonidandel, coach of Team Brazil and director of Socialdroids Robotics, China's efforts to apply humanoid robots to increasingly complex and practical tasks are particularly noteworthy.
"We need to put robots through increasingly demanding and complex challenges so that they can serve society," he explained.
This approach is reflected in this year's WHRG. In addition to competitive events such as soccer and athletics, the showpiece features 21 scenario-based events covering nine types of real-world needs, namely household and hospitality services, industrial production, emergency response, library management, retail, office services, green-space inspection and vehicle charging.
China is now home to over 140 humanoid robot manufacturers. With an annual shipment volume of 14,400 units, the country now accounts for eight out of every ten humanoid robots produced globally.
Tonidandel believes that clear support policies, competitions such as the WHRG and a steady influx of new talent are important factors behind the rapid development of humanoid robotics in China.
"You see university students, researchers and engineers are all deeply involved in the development of these robots," he said.
As humanoid robots begin to enter real-world applications, Tonidandel also sees greater room for cooperation between Brazil and China.
"Brazilians are faced with some challenges that Chinese may not be, and vice versa. The algorithms we develop in Brazil need to be adapted to local needs in Brazil," he said.
In his view, such cooperation could allow Brazilian researchers to learn from advanced technologies while helping Chinese robots develop solutions that can be applied in more countries.
"This collaboration is very important for both sides. Ultimately, it might facilitate applications of humanoid robots around the world," he said. ■

articles.title: 2 UN peacekeepers killed in an ambush in South Sudan
articles.body:
2 UN peacekeepers killed in an ambush in South Sudan
JUBA, South Sudan (AP) — Two United Nations peacekeepers were killed on Monday when armed men ambushed a patrol traveling to a remote area of South Sudan, according to the United Nations Mission in South Sudan.
Others injured in the attack by unidentified people included three peacekeepers, two members of the South Sudanese police and two civilian staff of the mission, UNMISS said in a statement.
The mission said it had deployed a “Quick Reaction Force” to secure the area and support the emergency response after the attack. The patrol was going to the area of Pajut in the state of Jonglei when it came under attack.
“Such deadly violence targeting UNMISS personnel who are serving to support peace in South Sudan is unacceptable,” Anita Kiki Gbeho, the head of UNMISS, said in the statement.
The identities and nationalities of the two peacekeepers killed were not immediately disclosed.
Violence is rampant in South Sudan, where government troops have been combating fighters and militias loyal to opposition leader Riek Machar, who was suspended last year as vice president after he faced charges of treason and other offenses he says are politically motivated. Attacks against peacekeepers are rare.
A 2018 peace deal between President Salva Kiir and Machar, who is under house arrest, has collapsed, leading to fears of a return to full-blown civil war.
More than 450 incidents of violence against humanitarian workers and assets were reported between January and July, more than double the number recorded during the same period last year, according to U.N. figures.
The conflict escalated in December when opposition forces seized government outposts in Jonglei. The government has conducted a counteroffensive since January with aerial bombardments and ground assaults, despite an official commitment to the peace agreement.
The U.S. has urged talks between Kiir and Machar. Earlier this year it called for “urgent action to uphold peace and mitigate the risk of civil war through an immediate return to dialogue among the parties to the 2018 peace agreement.”

articles.title: Denmark’s prime minister blasts unsolicited beauty advice from plastic surgeon on Instagram
articles.body:
Denmark’s prime minister blasts unsolicited beauty advice from plastic surgeon on Instagram
COPENHAGEN, Denmark (AP) — Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen is fed up with getting unsolicited beauty advice.
The 48-year-old wrote Monday on Instagram that she had just returned back home from a trip to Ukraine, where she was exposed to air raid sirens in the ongoing war, only to find a message by a plastic surgeon offering her to “fix that little spot on your nose.”
“I’ve lost count of how many messages I’ve received over the years about my appearance,” Frederiksen wrote. “Especially that I have ugly teeth and thin hair. That I have an ugly ‘wart’ on my nose and well-meaning advice to get some Botox.”
The prime minister of the Nordic country posted a screen shot of the plastic surgeon’s offer on Instagram but without identifying him.
She also posted her response: “Oh no. I’m happy with my body — I really don’t need a male plastic surgeon to have an opinion about it!”
Frederiksen, a Social Democrat and Denmark ’s second female prime minister, is now in her third term, making her one of Europe’s longest-serving and most experienced leaders. She has led the European Union and NATO member country since mid-2019.
She has pledged to maintain a firm stance against U.S. President Donald Trump’s ambitions for Greenland, the kingdom’s semiautonomous territory, and continue supporting Ukraine against Russia’s war of aggression.
On Instagram, Frederiksen stressed that she does not interfere with other people’s looks and that “I’m perfectly fine with my body — as it is when you’re a woman approaching 50.”
She added that “if you’re going to write to me (and you’re more than welcome to), I hope you’ll use your time to talk about something more meaningful. Not my nose.”
The prime minister also said that those unsolicited beauty tips and suggestions made her feel “indignant” and that “today, I’m sending an extra loving thought to all of you who have to put up with the ‘perfect imperfections’ we all walk around with every day.”

articles.title: Study finds AI chatbots can conduct basic therapy sessions but struggle to adapt to individual needs
articles.body:
A recent study published in the journal Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans suggests that artificial intelligence chatbots can conduct basic therapeutic conversations, though they struggle to consistently apply specific treatment techniques. The research indicates that a language model performed similarly to human practitioners in high-quality research settings, but its ability to adapt specialized psychological methods to individual needs remains inconsistent.
The global shortage of accessible mental health care has led experts to consider technology as a possible bridge. According to global health estimates cited by the study authors, hundreds of millions of individuals live with mental health conditions, yet structural barriers like cost and geographic distance leave the vast majority without professional care.
For example, the authors of a 2024 framework published in npj Mental Health Research argued that large language models hold tremendous potential to expand access to personalized treatments. A large language model (also known as an LLM) is a type of artificial intelligence trained on vast amounts of text, allowing it to generate human-like responses to prompts.
The authors of the 2024 paper proposed a roadmap for integrating these systems into clinical care, noting that psychotherapy is a high-stakes environment requiring nuanced expertise and responsible development. Despite this optimism, the actual clinical skills of these language models have remained largely untested in real-world scenarios. Previous research mostly relied on giving chatbots brief, fictional scenarios and asking human judges to rate the isolated responses for empathy or helpfulness.
These brief tests provide little insight into whether a computer program can manage a full, goal-directed therapy session that requires a coherent strategy. In a real session, a practitioner must dynamically adjust to the user’s changing emotional state and guide the conversation toward a beneficial outcome. This gap in knowledge motivated the authors of the new study to evaluate how well a language model actually performs when conducting a live, uninterrupted therapy session with a human user.
“Previous research had mostly examined LLM-chatbots’ skill at doing therapy by having them generate brief therapeutic responses or short excerpts of sessions, often in reply to a narrow set of client problems,” said study author Arthur Bran Herbener, a researcher at the Department of Psychology and Behavioral Sciences at Aarhus University. “We needed research that examines how skillfully LLM-chatbots can carry out full cognitive behavioral therapy sessions and adapt treatment to different individuals, using well-established, standardized metrics of therapeutic competence.”
To explore this question, the researchers designed an observational study involving 65 university students. These participants were experiencing mild to moderate psychological distress, such as presentation anxiety, occasional worrying, or perfectionism. Students with severe distress or diagnosed mental health disorders were excluded to ensure participant safety, as language models can sometimes generate unpredictable or inappropriate responses. Each participant completed a single 30-minute in-person session with a locally hosted artificial intelligence chatbot, exchanging an average of 49 messages.
The chatbot was programmed to deliver Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, a widely used, problem-oriented treatment that helps individuals identify and change unhelpful thoughts and behaviors. The researchers configured a specific language model to progress through the typical phases of a session. Rather than giving the chatbot a static set of rules, the researchers used a secondary background model to monitor the ongoing conversation. This secondary model evaluated the elapsed time and the current context, guiding the primary chatbot to shift from establishing a connection to conceptualizing the problem, applying an intervention, and finally wrapping up the conversation politely.
After the sessions concluded, trained graduate students read the conversation transcripts and rated the chatbot’s performance using the Cognitive Therapy Scale. This standardized assessment tool measures two main areas of clinical proficiency. The first area covers general therapeutic skills, such as expressing warmth and understanding. The second area covers specific skills, such as applying targeted techniques and guiding the user toward new insights.
To provide a benchmark for the chatbot’s scores, the researchers also conducted a meta-analysis of 18 prior studies that used the exact same scale to evaluate human practitioners. A meta-analysis is a statistical technique that combines the data from multiple independent studies to find an overall average or trend. This technique allowed the researchers to compare the chatbot’s performance to an established baseline of human competence.
The researchers found that the chatbot’s overall competence score fell slightly below the generally accepted threshold for adequate clinical performance. The standard rating scale defines an acceptable level of competence as a score of 40 out of a possible 66 points. The chatbot achieved this minimum threshold in 30 of the 65 sessions, showing a high degree of variability from one conversation to the next.
“We were surprised by how much variation the LLM-chatbot showed in its skillfulness across CBT sessions,” Herbener told PsyPost. “This is an important observation, as it suggests that we need research to ensure consistently competent care across individuals, and to understand when and why performance dips.”
When compared to the broad pool of human practitioners from the meta-analysis, the chatbot scored somewhat lower overall. The human professionals scored an average of 40.3 points on the rating scale, compared to the chatbot’s adjusted score of 38.1 points. However, the performance gap disappeared when the researchers looked only at the most rigorously conducted human studies. Compared to the six human studies judged to be of high methodological quality, the chatbot’s scores exhibited no statistically significant difference.
A closer look at the types of skills displayed by the chatbot highlighted a distinct pattern in its capabilities. The artificial intelligence performed better than human practitioners in general therapeutic skills, such as communicating empathy, validating the user’s feelings, and fostering a collaborative environment. In contrast, the chatbot struggled with the specific, technical skills required for this highly structured type of therapy. It had difficulty reliably identifying key beliefs, guiding the user through self-discovery, and adapting intervention strategies to fit the unique characteristics of each participant.
These technical struggles highlight the difference between following a predetermined structure and tailoring a method to a specific person. “LLM-chatbots designed to deliver therapy show promise in adhering to the cognitive behavioral treatment protocol, but there may be challenges in adapting to different individuals,” Herbener explained. “It’s also worth noting that good observable skill in delivering therapy is not the same as clinical effectiveness.”
“Effectiveness likely depends on factors beyond observable skill, such as positive expectations and a strong therapeutic relationship,” Herbener continued. “More comprehensive assessments of LLM-chatbots’ therapeutic competence may also require entirely new assessment approaches that account for LLMs’ distinct behavioral tendencies — such as sycophancy, or a tendency to excessively affirm users. Understanding this is crucial, since the ability to challenge clients’ beliefs is often considered important for fostering clinical change.”
These findings do not indicate that artificial intelligence is ready to replace human practitioners. The study evaluated the chatbot based on a single session with young adults experiencing only mild distress. Clinical populations often present more complex challenges, including severe hopelessness or safety risks. These complex cases place much higher demands on a practitioner’s ability to adapt and respond skillfully to unpredictability.
A single session also cannot capture the long-term planning, homework review, and relationship-building required in a complete, multi-week treatment program. In addition, the study faced challenges in consistently rating the chatbot’s text-based transcripts. The standard rating scale was originally designed for video or audio recordings, where raters can hear tone of voice and observe body language. Applying this tool to text may have made certain interpersonal skills harder to judge accurately.
Raters also knew they were evaluating an artificial intelligence, which may have influenced their scoring. In real-world applications, this lack of blinding reflects how users will actually interact with known computer systems, but it complicates direct comparisons to human professionals.
The researchers also caution against drawing overly broad conclusions from the matched scores between the chatbot and high-quality human studies. “Showing similar competence levels in CBT between human therapists and an LLM-chatbot does not mean they are equally effective ‘therapists’, nor that they are equally competent in an absolute sense,” Herbener said.
Because the human data came from past studies rather than a side-by-side test, the comparison remains indirect. “We did not directly compare the chatbot and human therapists in an experimental setting, so several factors beyond competence could bias our measurements,” Herbener added. “For example, the severity and type of psychological problems presented, or the norms for inferring behavioral observations clinicians and researchers apply when using the competence scale we relied on.”
To advance the field, future research will need to examine how chatbots perform across multiple sessions with clinical populations and investigate exactly why they sometimes fail to apply specific therapeutic techniques. “Research on LLM-chatbots in mental healthcare is still at a very early stage,” Herbener said. “Alongside design efforts aimed at ensuring consistently competent care, I’m also working to better understand the therapeutic relationship in LLM-based mental healthcare.”
Even if a chatbot can say all the right things, a user’s awareness that they are talking to a machine might alter the impact of those words. “We not only need to know how well these systems mimic human therapists’ language. We also need to understand what meaning clients attribute to that language once they know it comes from a machine,” Herbener explained. “Does the positive regard expressed by a chatbot serve the same clinical function as when it comes from a human? That’s one of the big open questions in the field.”
The study, “Exploring the therapeutic competencies of large language models: Observational study and comparison with meta-analytical estimates for human therapists,” was authored by Arthur Bran Herbener, Robert Zachariae, Michal Klincewicz, Mikkel Berg Thøgersen, Marie Rosenkrantz Hermann, and Malene Flensborg Damholdt.

articles.title: Kerman’s Pateh has potential to become global brand: official
articles.body:
Kerman’s Pateh has potential to become global brand: official
TEHRAN – Pateh, a traditional embroidered handicraft deeply rooted in the history and cultural identity of Iran’s Kerman province, has the potential to become a recognized global brand if commercialization, branding and market development are strengthened, a provincial handicrafts official said.
“Pateh is not merely a handicraft product, but a rooted art that is intertwined with the history and culture of Kerman and reflects an important part of the province’s cultural and artistic heritage,” Kerman’s deputy handicrafts chief Gholamreza Farrokhi said.
The official added that the craft has been passed down through generations within families and local communities, with this continuity playing an important role in preserving its authenticity and ensuring its cultural reproduction.
Pateh is a hand-stitched art form largely based on the skills and creativity of women in Kerman. Farrokhi said supporting the craft could help generate income for families, strengthen the local economy and expand home-based employment.
He stressed the need to give greater attention to the commercialization of Pateh while preserving its authenticity and quality. Market-oriented designs, professional packaging, standardization, marketing and the creation of sales networks could increase the added value of Pateh products and strengthen the livelihoods of artisans, he said.
Professional and targeted branding is also essential for promoting Pateh nationally and internationally, Farrokhi added. A distinctive visual identity, a clear narrative, a credible trademark and an appropriate marketing strategy could make the craft more recognizable in target markets and facilitate its entry into international markets.
“Pateh of Kerman has the potential to become a well-known brand,” he said, adding that artisans, economic operators, private-sector companies and specialized handicraft organizations could work together to establish an integrated production, distribution and export chain.
Farrokhi cautioned that expanding the Pateh market should not come at the expense of its authenticity. The goal, he said, should be to balance preservation of the craft’s identity with contemporary market demands by maintaining traditional characteristics while developing diverse and functional products suited to modern consumers.
He also called for greater promotion of Pateh through specialized exhibitions, cultural events and target markets, as well as through e-commerce and new media. Stronger links between artisans and commercial operators, along with improved packaging and presentation, could further raise awareness of the craft in domestic and international markets.
Pateh Douzi, in which colorful stitches cover much of the surface of a textile, is among Kerman’s best-known traditional handicrafts and souvenirs.
Because textiles are vulnerable to deterioration, few ancient Pateh pieces have survived. However, accounts and travel documents dating to the Safavid era indicate that the craft was practiced in Kerman at the time. One of the oldest surviving examples, dating to around 1869, was used as a cover for the tombstone of Shah Nematollah Vali, the Persian Sufi master and poet who lived in the 14th and 15th centuries.
Farrokhi described Pateh as a “living heritage” that connects Kerman’s past with the present and future, saying intelligent branding and commercialization could help transform the traditional art from a valued local craft into a product with a recognizable international identity.

articles.title: West turns Ukraine into 'frontier country' making money on war — economist
articles.body:
MOSCOW, August 24. /TASS/. The West has transformed Ukraine into a "frontier nation," whose sole purpose appears to be waging war while relying heavily on foreign aid, according to Oleg Pendzin, executive director of the Ukrainian Economic Discussion Club, who was speaking in an interview with the UNIAN news agency.
"From day one of the conflict, we've been fighting on borrowed money," Pendzin stated. "The socio-political climate surrounding us is causing significant concerns among our European partners regarding their own futures. Essentially, they are buying off Ukrainian blood."
Pendzin pointed out that Europe seems intent on shifting the entire burden of the conflict onto Ukrainian shoulders by funneling money and weapons into the country. He described Ukraine as a "frontier country" that exists solely through financial injections, aid, mercenaries, and weaponry - serving as a shield rather than an independent nation.
"Ukraine cannot survive solely on its own resources at this point," he emphasized. "Imagine if we didn't have access to the recent 90 billion euros from the EU lending program - our entire social system would collapse instantly. There would be no social assistance, no salaries for public sector workers, no aid for the impoverished, no pensions."
For several years, Ukraine's budget has been plagued by a record deficit. Domestic revenues no longer fully cover even military expenses, with Western aid filling the gap for most other expenditures. Kiev openly admits that its own financial resources are exhausted, and securing additional funding is increasingly challenging. Meanwhile, Western partners, including the IMF, are urging Ukrainian authorities to explore new avenues of self-financing, such as tightening tax policies. As former Ukrainian Prime Minister Nikolay Azarov (2010-2014) warned, without continued Western lending, Ukraine risks ceasing to exist as a functioning state.

articles.title: Surprise protests, GenZ outreach: Rahul Gandhi's new playbook after CJP's success
articles.body:
Surprise protests, GenZ outreach: Rahul Gandhi's new playbook after CJP's success
Priyanka Mukherjee / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 24, 2026, 20:33 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
Rahul Gandhi's new playbook shows a more persistent style, combining youth outreach, and surprise street protests.
NEW DELHI: "I will not leave till you lodge an FIR. He has pellet injuries on his body, has lost his eye, and we are demanding an FIR for this… I will go outside and sit there until you lodge an FIR. I will sit for 10 days, 20 days, 30 days, 50 days, six months. Your government will have a problem."There is a visible change in how Rahul Gandhi pushes through issues now. The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha has a new weapon in his political arsenal: impromptu protests.For the second time in a month, the Congress leader caught the authorities and, to some extent, even his own party, off guard by taking to the streets of the national capital without prior warning.When Rahul reached the DCP office in Delhi on August 21 demanding an FIR for Sahil Lohchab, who sustained pellet injuries during the July 20 student protest, it was Act 2 of his new playbook of street protest politics.When the cops dilly-dallied, Rahul refused to budge and staged a sit-in protest outside the police station. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined him. Congress leaders began arriving. Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed outside.
A visit to a police office turned into a high-voltage political stand-off and, after six hours of dharna, Delhi Police registered an FIR over the pellet firing.
'Politics of anarchy'
The BJP reacted sharply, calling Rahul's sit-in the 'politics of anarchy'. It argued that an FIR relating to the wider July 20 incident already existed, an investigation was under way and the Congress leader was turning police procedure into a political spectacle.For Lohchab, however, there was a sense of relief. His family had been trying to get his complaint registered since August 14, shuttling between police stations. The 19-year-old, who underwent surgery after pellets struck his right eye, finally had an FIR registered after Rahul’s intervention.For years, opponents have labelled Rahul Gandhi a 'part-time politician' who would raise an issue and then disappear. But this incident reinforced something that has changed about Rahul’s tactics over the past year. He is no longer content merely to raise an issue. He increasingly wants to enter it, stay with it and, if necessary, physically occupy the space.
Rahul's new playbook
The first display of this surprise street-politics instinct had come a month earlier during the NEET student protests.On July 21, a day after police used force to stop thousands of students attempting a 'Sansad Chalo' march over exam irregularities, Rahul suddenly headed towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence and staged a sit-in.Police had reportedly made arrangements anticipating a Congress protest at Vijay Chowk. Rahul went to Lok Kalyan Marg instead. The move caught security officials by surprise. Rahul, Priyanka and several other opposition leaders were later detained. The visual that immediately took over the news was hard to ignore: the leader of opposition physically struggling with police officers, being dragged away and getting a nosebleed in the chaos.
Police personnel detained Rahul Gandhi during a sit-in protest near the Prime Minister's residence.
That was Act 1.It came at a time when the Congress was desperately trying to make its presence felt, with Abhijeet Dipke’s Cockroach Janata Party and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk already leading a massive student protest against the NEET paper leak.Congress had initially kept its distance, preferring to run its own youth outreach campaign, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj'. But people asked a simple question: If Congress claimed to support student issues, why was it missing from the biggest student movement in Delhi?When the July 20 Jantar Mantar protest took place and massive outrage erupted over police action against the student protesters, Rahul's approach changed.The very next day, he moved to the front lines. He stood outside the Prime Minister's house, Congress leaders visited injured students, and police action became a major national debate. Rahul took the issue to Parliament and continued raising the pitch over injuries suffered by students.And when the larger protest began to recede from the headlines, Rahul stayed with one part of it: the use of pellet guns. He has affirmed that his party will keep raising the issue and demand accountability.
Rahul's changing style
The first major image makeover was when Rahul Gandhi embarked on the 'Bharat Jodo Yatra' from Kanyakumari to Kashmir in 2022. Sceptics and rivals wondered if he would complete the journey. By the time he reached Kashmir months later, after walking thousands of kilometres in his now-signature white T-shirt, one charge had become considerably harder to make: that Rahul was unwilling to put in the physical grind that it takes in politics.The yatra, on its own, did not help the Congress much. What it did was change the way Rahul himself was seen as a politician.For months, people saw him walking with the common public rather than delivering a scripted speech from a podium. He met farmers, labourers and students, stopped for conversations, entered homes and sat and ate with people.The yatra experience also laid the foundation for his growing social media popularity. His online presence today increasingly relies on short, conversational exchanges that can easily travel as reels and clips.The second shift came in 2024, when he became the leader of the opposition.Since then, we have seen a more combative Rahul Gandhi. Whether one agrees with his politics or the issues he raises, he appears considerably more comfortable with confrontation than he once did.Congress's protests in the Parliament complex have also become more visual and experimental under Rahul.He repeatedly joined opposition MPs at Makar Dwar over the Election Commission’s SIR exercise in Bihar, with MPs carrying 'vote chori' placards and demanding its rollback. The protest later moved beyond the Parliament gates, with Rahul and other opposition leaders marching towards the Election Commission before being stopped and detained.Rahul provokes ministers across the aisle and stays for the response. He takes an argument from the street into Parliament and, increasingly, carries it back outside again. This is also a part of his renewed Gen Z outreach.
'Chhatron Ki Goonj'
If Bharat Jodo helped Rahul Gandhi build the image of a politician who was more approachable and willing to listen, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' took that idea to a more specific audience: Gen Z.The programme began in Kota, where students spoke about paper leaks, recruitment delays, coaching pressure and the uncertainty around exams and jobs. The format was less rally and more conversation, with Rahul asking questions, listening, and allowing individual experiences to shape the message. That made the outreach more relatable.His latest Pune edition further widened that outreach by putting young women at the centre of the conversation.
Rahul's call to 'smash the patriarchy' in a stadium full of women was a strong message that came with its own set of criticism. He spoke about different social expectations for boys and girls, cited the 'Manusmriti' while attacking the BJP-RSS worldview, and told women that they 'belong' to themselves rather than to fathers, husbands or sons, triggering huge applause from the crowd.While a large section of people lauded the focus on women, the ruling BJP immediately trained its guns on him and asked him to induct women ministers into the Karnataka cabinet, where Congress is in power.
The Jharkhand dilemma
Even as Rahul attacked the BJP over issues such as NEET and paper leaks, major student protests broke out in Jharkhand, where the Congress shares power in the Hemant Soren government. Soon after the Jantar Mantar agitation ended, aspirants took to the streets in Ranchi over alleged irregularities and paper leaks in JPSC and JSSC examinations.This time, the criticism was closer to home. Protesters targeted not just chief minister Hemant Soren but Rahul as well, pointing to the irony of him speaking for students nationally while Congress was part of the ruling alliance in Jharkhand. Effigies of both leaders were burnt, and Rahul was accused of not speaking about Jharkhand issues.Eventually, Rahul was forced to react and intervene. He asserted that Congress supported students protesting peacefully and said that dialogue was the only way forward.Rahul wrote an open letter to Soren, requesting the CM to personally meet the students and hear out their grievances. The Jharkhand government later accepted the students' demands.The episode helped Rahul avoid the charge of being selective on student issues, but it also showed the challenge of claiming an issue as your own: once you do that, you can be questioned even when the government under fire is run by an ally.
Has Rahul evolved as a leader?
For years, Rahul Gandhi was accused of being an inconsistent politician who would raise important issues and then disappear from the conversation. Rivals branded him as an “entitled leader” and took “Pappu” digs at him.
But the old image of Rahul as a reluctant politician is certainly harder to sustain today. From Bharat Jodo to 'Chhatron Ki Goonj', fiery parliamentary confrontations and surprise dharnas, he appears more comfortable playing on the front foot.However, his latest round of street protests seems to stem from the crisis that the opposition in general and Congress in particular faced as Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP mobilised youth in large numbers and forced the government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign as Union education minister.Rahul has made his presence felt, but we will have to wait and see if his new politics translates into electoral success for the Congress.
Priyanka Mukherjee is an Assistant News Editor at The Times of India, where deadlines rarely slow down. Often juggling breaking news, long-form explainers and the everyday chaos of the newsroom, she is usually managing stress, chasing clarity and trying to log off on time (rarely successful). She also cares deeply about stories around women’s rights and social change, while two very opinionated dogs make sure she never truly switches off.

articles.title: Syria struggling to deal with attacks on security forces
articles.body:
Breadcrumb
Syria struggling to deal with attacks on security forces
Although the intensity of military confrontations has declined across most of Syria, attacks targeting security and military forces continue to occur, following a pattern of smaller, asymmetric operations. These range from bus bombings and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) to individual assassinations and ambushes.
Available information indicates that a large proportion of these attacks are linked to cells affiliated with Islamic State group. Responsibility for other attacks remains unknown, amid speculation about involvement of groups linked to remnants of the Assad regime.
Since Assad’s ouster in December 2024, ISIS has called on its members to fight the new government led by President Ahmad al-Sharaa, which has joined the US-led international coalition against the organisation.
Overnight buses targeted
Incidents recorded over the past year reveal a clear focus on buses transporting security and military personnel, as they are targets that bring together large numbers of personnel at a specific time and place.
The most recent such attack occurred on Saturday, when a bus belonging to the Internal Security Forces hit an IED on a road in the Damascus countryside, injuring several security personnel.
This came two weeks after a passenger bus was bombed in Jaramana, near Damascus, killing a woman and injuring 13 people.
A similar incident occurred in northeastern Syria in May, when two soldiers were killed in an attack on a military transport bus.
The most high-profile attack came during Emmanuel Macron's visit to the country in July, when Damascus was hit by twin blasts close to the French president's hotel. The interior ministry blamed ISIS which it said had planted explosives in a vehicle and a rubbish container.
Rashid Hourani, a researcher at the Jusoor Centre for Studies, told The New Arab that the targeting of vehicles belonging to the interior and defence ministries reveals weaknesses in security procedures. He also pointed to the sectarian nature of some of the attacks, highlighting the targeting of areas with high Alawite and Christian populations.
A security source who requested anonymity told The New Arab that most bombings and attacks have increasingly focused on overnight buses because they are relatively easy targets. They also believe that requiring personnel to surrender their weapons while on leave may also have increased their vulnerability to attack.
The source suggests providing personnel with weapons or security protection while they are traveling, avoiding the wearing of military uniforms while on leave, and changing travel routes and schedules.
He warned that some attacks may be random and primarily intended to create confusion and embarrass the government.
Assassinations, ambushes
Security forces have also come under fire from assailants in areas of eastern and northern Syria in recent months.
The latest such incidents came on Friday when a soldier and a member of the security forces were killed in separate attacks in Hama and Aleppo.
In recent months, there have also been attacks targeting personnel while they were traveling or outside their duty stations. In May, an attack on a defence ministry facility in Damascus killed one soldier and injured 23 people. Meanwhile, ISIS claimed responsibility for an attack in Hasakah that killed two soldiers.
ISIS also claimed responsibility for detonating a sticky bomb targeting the car of the head of the Justice Department in Babila, Salah Ahmad al-Saleh, seriously injuring him.
The extremist group has intensified its attacks against government forces since the beginning of the year. 29 people, including 23 military personnel, were killed in more than 30 ISIS attacks between 17 February and 19 March. The attacks were concentrated primarily in Deir ez-Zour, Raqqa, and Aleppo, with other incidents recorded in Idlib, Hasakah, and Homs.
Shifting threats
In response, the Syrian authorities have intensified their campaigns against ISIS cells. The Interior Ministry announced earlier this month that it had arrested a senior military commander the Manbij countryside. Last July, the authorities announced operations in Aleppo and Latakia that resulted in the arrest of ISIS members and the seizure of weapons.
The ministry said in June that over a three-month period it had arrested 235 people on terrorism charges and thwarted seven attacks that it said ISIS had been planning.
Military experts partly attribute this to the sensitivity of the transitional period and the presence of operational gaps resulting from the process of integrating the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) and other local groups into the army and security forces.
The record of the past year reveals that armed groups have shifted towards trying to wear down government forces through low-level bombings, assassinations, and ambushes.
The most prominent vulnerabilities include the predictable routes and schedules of overnight buses, personnel being exposed while on leave, and the difficulty of controlling open terrain and remote areas.
Major Khaled Abdullah, director of the Interior Minister’s office, said in press statements that the defence and interior ministries have issued directives prohibiting the wearing of official uniforms outside working hours and strengthening security measures. He noted that security and military institutions are working on other solutions to reduce risks.

articles.title: US to double tariffs on Canadian vehicles after trade talks break down, Trump says
articles.body:
"Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years," the president wrote in a post on his Truth Social account.
US President Donald Trump announced on Monday that the US would double tariffs on Canadian vehicles from 2027 as he accused Ottawa of "ripping off the United States of America for years."
In a post on his Truth Social account, Trump wrote: "On January First, 2027, Tariffs on all Cars, Trucks, both large and small, Automotive Parts, and Steel, will be increased to 50%."
Current US tariff rates on automobiles stand at 25% for non-US content.
The threats come amid a growing trade war between the two neighbours that hit a flash point on Friday after talks over a deal to avoid 50% duties on some Canadian goods collapsed as both sides accused each other of trying to implement last-minute changes.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada had been forced to walk away from the "bad" deal as "we cannot accept what they've offered, and we will not give what they've asked."
The levies, which came into effect on Saturday, impact around $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.
Carney warned that Ottawa would match the US tariffs "dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses."
"Our response will be concentrated in sectors such as steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics," Carney added in a speech on Saturday.
The Office of the United States Trade Representative described the breakdown in talks as a "missed opportunity" for Canada, which it said was maintaining a "prolonged retaliation" against the US.
"Despite the U.S. offer to Canada to receive the best treatment of any major exporter to our market, new demands and walk backs of other commitments by Canada have upended the careful balance reached in the past days," it said.
Trump's tariff strategy
On Monday, Trump also lashed out at what he called Canada's "ridiculously high tariffs" on US farmers and said the country would no longer be treated "like a state."
Trump has repeatedly suggested that Canada should become the US' "51st state" and said last week that Ottawa wanted "the benefits of being a State, without being one."
The American president has pursued an aggressive tariff policy during his second stint in the White House, raising levies on partners across the world. The administration argues that tariffs will boost US manufacturing and encourage domestic job growth while addressing what it sees as unfair trade rates.
Critics, however, say increasing duties are making life more expensive for American consumers and businesses while fostering widespread uncertainty among companies planning investments and supply chains.

articles.title: Venice Film Festival adds Gaza doc ‘NAZA’ to competition lineup
articles.body:
Venice Film Festival adds Gaza doc ‘NAZA’ to competition lineup
The Venice Film Festival has added a new documentary about the civilian toll of the Israel-Hamas war to its lineup. “NAZA,” from two of the filmmakers behind the Oscar-winning documentary “No Other Land,” will screen in the main competition, festival organizers said Monday.
According to the synopsis, the film was shot at night on Tel Aviv rooftops and focuses on the killings of Palestinian civilians. Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor co-directed “Naza,” which was produced by The Guardian and filmmakers behind “The Zone of Interest.” It’s the only documentary competing for the Golden Lion award.
Abraham and Szor were two of the four directors of the 2025 best documentary winner “No Other Land,” the story of Palestinian activists fighting to protect their communities from demolition by the Israeli military. A collaboration between Israeli and Palestinian filmmakers, it was made over four years between 2019 and 2023, wrapping production days before Hamas launched its deadly Oct. 7, 2023 attack on Israel that started the war in Gaza.
“Naza” builds on reporting between 2023 and 2025 published by the Israeli-Palestinian +972 Magazine, the Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and The Guardian.
The war was top of mind at last year’s festival as well, where thousands gathered for a large pro-Palestinian protest during one of the busiest nights in hopes of redirecting the spotlight from the movie stars to the real world. The subject was also prominent in the program: Kaouther Ben Hania’s “The Voice of Hind Rajab,” about the death of a 6-year-old girl attempting to flee Gaza City with her family in early 2024, won the festival’s Silver Lion award.
Ben Hania is part of the Maggie Gyllenhaal-led jury that will be selecting the award winners at the festival, which begins on Sept. 2. Winners will be announced on Sept. 12.
Earlier this year, the Venice Biennale contemporary art exhibition opened with no Golden Lions after the jury quit in protest of Israel’s and Russia’s participation and loud protests outside their pavilions. In 2024 the artist and curators representing Israel at the Venice Biennale kept the Israeli pavilion exhibit closed, saying they would only open it if there were a ceasefire in Gaza.

articles.title: Gang coalition unleashes violent new attack on farming community in Haiti
articles.body:
Gang coalition unleashes violent new attack on farming community in Haiti
PORT-AU-PRINCE, Haiti (AP) — A powerful gang coalition attacked a once peaceful farming community nestled in the hills above Haiti’s capital, killing multiple people, an official told The Associated Press on Monday.
Kenscoff Mayor Jean Massillon said armed men raided the community late Sunday, setting fire to homes and killing residents.
“It is still impossible to establish a definitive death toll due to access difficulties and communication problems,” he said.
Wails filled the air in Kenscoff as survivors found the bodies of friends and family strewn on the streets early Monday.
Farmer Mathurin Pierre, 41, told The Associated Press that he lost 14 loved ones and that an unknown number remain missing.
Massillon blamed the attack on members of Viv Ansanm, which the U.S. government designated as a foreign terrorist organization last year.
“They sowed chaos,” Massillon said.
He said gang members targeted a church and homes including those owned by Dr. Jean “Bill” Pape. He is a renowned doctor who runs a non-governmental organization in Haiti that helps patients including those with HIV and tuberculosis.
No further details about the attack were available. A spokesperson for the U.N.-backed gang suppression force did not immediately return a message seeking comment.
Gangs control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince, the capital, with Viv Ansanm repeatedly targeting nearby Kenscoff.
Gang violence has displaced a record 1.5 million people across Haiti, where more than 3,100 people were reported killed from January to June and another 1,189 injured, according to U.N. statistics.
The attack comes less than a week after the U.S. government deported more than 160 people to the troubled Caribbean country for the first time since the Trump administration won a legal battle to end Temporary Protected Status for some 350,000 Haitians.
Haiti is scheduled to hold general elections for the first time in more than a decade on Dec. 13, and it has been registering voters in Port-au-Prince and beyond. Experts have warned it’s currently too dangerous to hold elections.
___
Associated Press reporter Dánica Coto in San Juan, Puerto Rico, contributed.

articles.body:
Mainland China’s ship activity near Taiwan hits record for third month in a row
Beijing has ramped up its law-enforcement and survey operations around island since Tokyo and Manila announced boundary talks
Taiwan’s defence ministry said that in the first 24 days of August it detected mainland coastguard, survey and other official vessels a total of 118 times, surpassing the 117 reported in July and 111 in June.
Those numbers were far higher than in any previous month on record since Taiwan began releasing detection data in July 2024. Before June, the highest count of mainland government ships in a single month was 50 in April 2025, according to a tally by the SCMP.
That record-breaking intensity of activity aligns with findings from an August 19 report by the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative (AMTI), which noted a “more sustained and assertive presence” by mainland Chinese law-enforcement and survey vessels in waters east of Taiwan.
Using commercial automatic identification system data, AMTI – a programme of the Washington-based Centre for Strategic and International Studies – showed that the ships’ activity around Taiwan between June and August was concentrated in waters where Chinese, Japanese and Philippine maritime claims overlap. Almost no such activity had been observed in that area between January and late May.
Two China Coast Guard vessels accounted for much of the observable activity during that period, while a third had been patrolling the area since August 4, according to AMTI. Within days of the Japan-Philippines announcement, mainland Chinese law-enforcement vessels hailed 198 commercial ships in the area, demanding information about their ports of call and crews, the report noted.
