articles.title: China delays ambitious Chang’e 7 moon mission until 2027
articles.body:
China’s lunar ambitions took a hit after the country called off the launch of a spacecraft that it has aimed to make the first to ever land on the moon’s south pole.
Chang’e 7 was supposed to launch onboard a Long March 5 rocket on August 24, but the launch was scrubbed on Sunday evening, China’s Manned Space Agency (CMSA) said in a statement. Poor weather conditions linked to Typhoon Narra were likely a factor. As a result, the mission will be put on ice until at least 2027.
The decision to delay the mission was reached after extensive review, the CMSA said, and reflects the need for “absolute safety.”
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
China and the U.S. are in a race to send humans back to the moon, a feat that that U.S. accomplished in the 1960s and that has never been achieved by any other country. Chang’e 7 is to play to a crucial part in China’s ambitions: the probe is designed to search for frozen water in the Shackleton Crater, a pit that spans some 21 kilometers (13 miles) and sits beside the lunar south pole.
No spacecraft has ever landed in that region, which scientists consider to be among the likeliest places to find water on the moon. Locating water that can be used by humans is vital to establishing any long-term lunar presence. NASA and China are eyeing the region to establish a crewed base—and because this real estate is so precious, it matters who gets their first.
NASA plans to establish a lunar colony by 2036, while China hopes to begin construction of the International Lunar Research Station, a moon base built in collaboration with Russia, in 2031. The CMSA has stated it aims to put humans on the lunar surface no later than 2030, while NASA’s Artemis IV mission to land humans on the moon for the first time in more than half a century is tentatively scheduled for early 2028.

articles.title: Helium balloon triggers explosions, train disruptions at Ben Gurion | Watch
articles.body:
A helium balloon drifted into the railway station at Ben Gurion International Airport on Monday afternoon, causing electrical cables to short circuit and producing several loud bangs that disrupted train service at the country’s main international airport.
Passengers reported hearing explosions before people on the platform were directed into the airport terminal. Platform 2 was temporarily closed to train traffic following the incident.
Israel Railways described the incident as a localized technical malfunction that was being repaired. Some trains halted their journeys before reaching their final destinations, while others were delayed.
“There was a localized malfunction that is currently being handled. Trains are running,” Israel Railways said. “There may be delays in the near future, but train traffic has not been halted.”
The company disputed reports that the airport railway station had been evacuated, saying it “was not evacuated of passengers and continues normal operations.”
‘There were three explosions’
One passenger who contacted ynet said an electrical cable had been severed and that the 3:09 p.m. train from Jerusalem to Herzliya became stranded several minutes before reaching Ben Gurion Airport.
“There was no electricity or air conditioning for 10 minutes,” the passenger said, adding that passengers were later informed that the train would return to Jerusalem.
Another passenger said the train stopped at the station before three loud explosions were heard. “They have now evacuated everyone from the platform to the terminal,” the passenger said.
Alex, who was aboard one of the trains at the time, told ynet that his train had already arrived at the airport station when he heard several explosions.
“We stopped at the station and then there were several sounds of explosions, and the cable for the train opposite us snapped and fell,” he said. “There were flashes of light from an electrical short circuit and then another explosion. They then announced over the public-address system that we had to evacuate the train and led everyone into Ben Gurion Airport.”
Because of the resulting disruptions, Alex left the station and continued his journey by bus.
A senior Israel Railways official offered a stark assessment of the incident, warning that the railway had repeatedly narrowly avoided a serious accident.
“Every time, only an obvious miracle saves civilians from a deadly disaster,” the official told ynet. “But everyone knows that even obvious miracles run out one day. Once again, they will look for a scapegoat to blame. The disaster will come; only the date is unknown.”
Leadership vacuum at Israel Railways
The disruption comes as Israel Railways, the state-owned company that operates the country’s passenger and freight rail network, has been without its two most senior permanent executives for nearly two months: a board chairman and a CEO.
Moshe Shimoni, who served as chairman for about six years, left the position last month after being appointed chairman of Mekorot, Israel’s national water company.
Meanwhile, nearly a year after CEO Moshe “Shiko” Zana left the railway, a permanent replacement has yet to be appointed. Avner Flor, a former head of the Transportation Ministry’s infrastructure administration, is serving as acting CEO.
Industry officials say the difficulty in filling the CEO position is unsurprising because it is considered one of the most complex management jobs in Israel’s public sector.
Along with overseeing infrastructure projects worth tens of billions of shekels, the railway’s chief executive must contend with a powerful workers union, operational failures that frequently cause service disruptions, safety incidents and accidents, as well as persistent public criticism over the quality and reliability of train service.
Years of management upheaval
Israel Railways has experienced significant management turnover in recent years.
During Shimoni’s tenure as chairman, two CEOs were replaced, while a string of senior executives left the company, including its chief financial officer, legal adviser, head of human resources and head of the railway electrification administration.
More recently, the executive responsible for freight operations was removed from his position following two freight-train accidents.
The company has also faced delays to its electrification program, the end of its contract with Spanish infrastructure company SEMI and operational challenges during the war with Iran.
The upheaval comes at a particularly consequential period for Israel’s railway network, which is preparing to operate and complete some of the largest infrastructure projects in its history.
They include the Eastern Railway, the Route 431 railway, a fourth track through Tel Aviv’s heavily congested Ayalon rail corridor and completion of the nationwide electrification project.
For now, Israel Railways continues to operate under interim leadership at a time when it is expected to carry out its most ambitious development plans while also working to restore public confidence in the reliability and safety of its service.

Ukraine has issued a unique commemorative silver coin marking the 35th anniversary of Independence

The 20-hryvnia coin is made of .925 sterling silver, with a mintage of up to 5,000 pieces. Its design symbolizes the protection of Ukraine’s freedom.
On Ukraine’s Independence Day, August 24, 2026, the National Bank of Ukraine put into circulation a commemorative coin “To the 35th Anniversary of Ukraine’s Independence,” UNN reports, citing the NBU.
Details
The coin continues the “Ukrainian State” series and is dedicated to the 35th anniversary of the proclamation of Ukraine’s independence—one of the most important events in the modern history of Ukrainian statehood, which embodied the Ukrainian people’s thousand-year aspiration for freedom.
The presentation of this unique silver commemorative coin took place in the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine. It was here that, 35 years ago, on August 24, 1991, the Act of Proclamation of Ukraine’s Independence was adopted.
“For the National Bank, every commemorative coin is an opportunity to speak through the language of symbols, remind people of what is important, and preserve memory. When we were looking for the image that most accurately embodies 35 years of Ukraine’s Independence, we chose a shield. It has been struck, but it has not broken; it has endured. This is a metaphor for Ukraine. And the hand of a Ukrainian warrior firmly holding this shield reminds us that independence is protected by people, by Ukrainian soldiers. They defend it for the sake of a future symbolized by a child’s drawing—simple, like all true values: a child, a heart, the sun, a home. We bow our heads before those who gave their lives for these values. We thank those who are defending them now,” emphasized Andriy Pyshnyy, Governor of the National Bank of Ukraine.
“Today demonstrated a very important component of our unity. Different parliamentarians, different people, different eras, but everyone has the same goal—to do everything so that Ukraine endures and Ukraine wins. This is the leitmotif for each of us. Great goals lie ahead of us, and we will certainly achieve them. And the grandeur of this moment must be preserved in symbols that will carry this information to future generations, including in Ukrainian currency,” noted Ruslan Stefanchuk, Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine.
About the coin’s design
The commemorative coin “To the 35th Anniversary of Ukraine’s Independence” has a face value of 20 hryvnias and is made of .925 sterling silver; its minting quality category is “special uncirculated,” and the weight of the precious metal in pure form is 62.2 g. The coin’s edge is smooth with recessed inscriptions. The coin is decorated with patination and selective gilding. Its mintage is up to 5 000 pieces.
The obverse of the coin depicts the hand of a serviceman holding a shield. At the top is an image of a child’s drawing that serves as a talisman for the defender. In the upper-left section is the inscription УКРАЇНА, while on the right are the small State Emblem of Ukraine, the year of minting—2026, the denomination 20, and the graphic hryvnia symbol ₴. The circular inscription reads: 35 РОКІВ БОРОТЬБИ ЗА МАЙБУТНЄ.
The reverse depicts the outer side of a shield with damage, symbolizing the struggle for the freedom and independence of the Ukrainian people.

articles.title: Firefighters are trying to stop a fast-moving Nevada wildfire from spreading to homes in Reno
articles.body:
Firefighters are trying to stop a fast-moving Nevada wildfire from spreading to homes in Reno
Live from Reno, Nevada, as firefighters try to bring the fast-moving Hawk Fire under control. Some 90,000 people have been told to evacuate as officials said the fire was “human-caused,” without providing details.
RENO, Nevada (AP) — A wildfire that mushroomed over the weekend in the Sierra Nevada foothills spread perilously close to neighborhoods in Reno, Nevada, forcing authorities to urge more than 90,000 residents to leave their homes.
The out-of-control fire has already burned some homes, but there’s concern that shifting winds could push the flames into newly developed and densely packed neighborhoods on the edge of Nevada’s second-biggest city.
Schools across the county were closed Monday because of the evacuations and to keep roads clear for emergency crews.
Authorities said late Sunday that the Hawk Fire had stayed in its footprint and firefighters were extinguishing hotspots while working to keep the fire from jumping a main highway and reaching areas filled with homes and businesses.
The fire began Saturday and grew to more than 23 square miles (60 square kilometers) on Sunday across foothills ringed by neighborhoods near the California state line. There was zero containment.
At least six people — three first responders and three civilians — were injured. Officials said the fire was “human-caused” but did not say whether it was intentionally set or accidental.
Videos posted on social media showed the smoldering ruins of homes and cars, with only a scorched basketball hoop still standing.
Many residents had little time to evacuate after the fire exploded in size.
“Honestly, I thought it was like in a movie,” said Ruby Delatorre, who got back from a concert only to find her home in the evacuation zone. She returned Sunday to walk to her home and get a few more possessions.
“I literally want to cry and go back for all my stuff. I just got what I thought I needed,” Delatorre said.
Some who spotted the smoke on Saturday thought it was from another wildfire that has been burning the past two weeks.
Teresa Lenshyn, who is among the evacuees, said being forced to leave was chaotic and stressful. “You don’t know if the winds are going to shift and it’s going to get worse,” she said.
The Hawk Fire is the third large wildfire in the rugged terrain north of Reno in the past two weeks — all caused by human activity, according to fire officials.
Extremely dry conditions across the American West have sparked a rash of wildfires this summer. Fires in eastern Washington state forced the evacuation of 60,000 people in the Spokane area in early August.
Nationwide, there have been more than 50,000 wildfires — the most over the past 10 years covering the same time period, according to the National Interagency Fire Center.
___
Seewer reported from Toledo, Ohio. Associated Press reporters John Raby in Charleston, West Virginia, and Jack Brook in New Orleans contributed.

Trump threatens 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks amid trade row
The two countries failed to reach a trade deal late on Friday, with each side blaming the other
US tariffs on all cars and trucks, automotive parts and steel would be increased to 50 per cent starting January 1 next year, President Donald Trump said in a social post on Monday after trade talks with Canada collapsed over the weekend.
“Build in the U.S. and there are ZERO TARIFFS. Canada will be treated like a State no longer!” Trump wrote.
“On Trade, and in other ways, also, they are among the worst Nations in the World to deal with. They feel entitled, and yet, WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!”
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment seeking more details on the threatened tariffs. Representatives for the Canadian government also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The two countries failed to reach a trade deal late on Friday, with each side blaming the other as Canada readied tariffs on some US goods in retaliation for 50 per cent levies ordered by Trump on other Canadian products.

articles.title: Dome installation begins at Shams Tabrizi mausoleum in Khoy
articles.body:
Dome installation begins at Shams Tabrizi mausoleum in Khoy
TEHRAN – The installation of the dome at the mausoleum of Shams Tabrizi in Khoy, a major architectural project in northwestern Iran, has begun, according to the director general of West Azarbaijan’s Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts Department.
Morteza Safari said on Monday that the project’s distinctive engineering and architectural features would make the dome a prominent urban landmark in Khoy.
The dome will have a total height of 15.5 meters, placing it among the tallest domes built in northwestern Iran, Safari said.
He added that the first phase of the project, involving construction of the concrete structure, had been completed, while work was continuing on a 9.5-meter-high steel framework.
The dome has been designed as a double-shell structure. Its exterior will feature traditional brickwork, while the interior will be decorated with plasterwork and karbandi, a traditional Iranian architectural technique involving geometric ornamental vaulting.
According to Safari, the brickwork has been inspired by historical periods and incorporates innovative, project-specific techniques intended to distinguish the structure from similar architectural projects.
The dome is expected to serve not only as an important cultural and memorial structure but also as an example of contemporary architectural and engineering achievement in northwestern Iran, he said.
Shams Tabrizi (1185–1248) was a 13th-century Persian mystic whose teachings profoundly influenced Jalal al-Din Rumi. He is the namesake of Rumi’s Divan-e Shams-e Tabrizi and is traditionally associated with Rumi’s spiritual transformation. Khoy, in West Azarbaijan province, has historically served as a crossroads of culture and commerce.

articles.title: Iran discovers major gas field "Takhteh" in Fars province worth $45b
articles.body:
Iran discovers major gas field "Takhteh" in Fars province worth $45b
TEHRAN- The Exploration Director of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) has announced that the newly discovered "Takhteh" gas field in Fars Province has an estimated economic value of approximately $45 billion, describing it as one of the most significant gas discoveries in the country over the past two decades.
In an interview with Shana, Seyyed Mohieddin Jafari detailed the discovery of the Takhteh gas field, stating that it is located 10 kilometers northwest of the city of Khonj and approximately 35 kilometers from the old gas fields of "Shanul" and "Homa."
He explained that the total gas in place at this field amounts to 7,500 billion cubic feet. With a recovery factor of 72%, approximately 5,700 billion cubic feet of this volume is recoverable.
Jafari noted that the gas from the Takhteh field is sweet, emphasizing: "This gas does not require a sweetening process, so it will follow a shorter path in development and processing compared to sour gas fields."
Equivalent to 15 years of production from one phase of South Pars
Jafari stated that the recoverable gas from Takhteh is equivalent to about 15 years of production from a standard phase of South Pars, and added: "This reserve can play a significant role in meeting the country's gas demand."
He announced that the field is about 50 kilometers long and 4 kilometers wide, and described it as "one of the most complex exploration structures discovered in the last 20 years" in terms of geological complexities.
Referring to the field's geological challenges, Jafari explained: "Multiple layer repetitions and faulting in the upstream sections of the reservoir made exploration operations highly difficult. Nevertheless, exploratory drilling continued to a depth of about five kilometers underground, and upon entering the reservoir, a significant volume of gas was discovered in a thickness of approximately 450 meters."
20 million barrels of recoverable condensates
Jafari also reported the presence of 27 million barrels of gas condensates in the Takhteh field, noting that about 20 million barrels of this amount are recoverable. Combined with the gas reserves, this brings the field's economic value to around $40 billion.
Regarding the exploration timeline, he said: "The drilling of the Takhteh exploratory well alone took about 17 months. After completing exploration operations and conducting final tests, the obtained data were carefully analyzed."
The Exploration Director of NIOC further emphasized that the entire exploration process of the Takhteh field was carried out by Iranian personnel, stating: "All exploration stages—from geological studies and geophysical activities to drilling operations—were conducted using the capabilities of Iranian forces."
Jafari added: "The technology, equipment, and tools used in this operation are also Iranian. In technical, equipment, and engineering sectors, there was no need for foreign personnel or companies."
He described the Takhteh gas field as a fully Iranian discovery and stressed: "This achievement demonstrates that the country's technical, engineering, and specialized capacity in oil and gas exploration has reached a level where complex exploration projects can be successfully completed without reliance on foreign parties."

articles.title: China urges relevant parties to stop political manipulation, interference in Hong Kong affairs: spokesperson
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- Hong Kong affairs are purely China's internal affairs and China urges relevant parties to earnestly respect China's sovereignty and the rule of law in Hong Kong, and stop the political manipulation and interference in the Hong Kong affairs and China's internal affairs in any form, a foreign ministry spokesperson said here Monday.
Spokesperson Lin Jian made the remarks after the EU and certain countries including the United States have expressed their concerns in their statements and remarks regarding the case that Hong Kong's High Court convicted the "Hong Kong Alliance" and its former leaders Lee Cheuk-yan, Ho Chun-yan and Chow Hang-tung of inciting subversion.
Certain countries and institutions used the judicial case to make malicious smears against Hong Kong and its rule of law, and interfered in China's internal affair, Lin said, adding China firmly opposes it and has lodged serious protests.
Pointing out that the platform of "Hong Kong Alliance" is aimed at subverting state power at its core, and the facts concerning the defendants' crimes are clear and the offense has caused serious harm, Lin said it's legitimate and lawful for the government of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) to combat the activities endangering national security.
"Hong Kong upholds rule of law. The central government firmly supports the Hong Kong SAR in safeguarding national security and combating activities that endanger national security in accordance with the law," he said. ■

articles.title: Music Review: Mike D 5D’s debut solo album ‘Thank You’ offers glitchy, post-Beastie Boy fun
articles.body:
Music Review: Mike D 5D’s debut solo album ‘Thank You’ offers glitchy, post-Beastie Boy fun
ATLANTA (AP) — Mike D 5D, a new project from former Beastie Boy Michael Diamond, will release “Thank You” on Friday — the debut solo album from the MC and the first new music from the Beastie Boys’ camp since the 2012 death of Adam “MCA” Yauch.
“Thank You” is a debut album unafraid to traverse new sonic ground — and suffers only the occasional misfire.
Joined by his band — his sons Skyler and Davis Diamond as well as Eddie Ruscha, Will Graefe and Milo Ruscha — Mike D’s album bristles with stuttering drum and bass breaks and distressed vocals on the opening tracks “Switch Up” and “What We Got,” both of which sound as if they were pushed through an overdrive pedal. Somehow it works and is fitting with Mike D 5D’s high-volume and energetic style.
Less necessary are meandering and repetitive songs such as “Secrets Pt. II,” in which Mike D discusses his discomfort. “I got secrets,” the rapper implores, repeatedly — no, seriously, a lot — while failing to reveal one. The rapper has a musical idea, but not much of a lyrical one.
Much of the album plays out like a man in a bedroom with a vintage synth, a half dozen beered-up friends and a laptop stuffed with aging drum software. Such is true of the track “Crypto,” which purports to cast a cautious eye at greed, but lurches melodically. Ultimately, it relents to a frenetic and fuzzy declaration from Mike D of “All these people in your ear, they’re in your ear / All these people talking in your ear, in your ear” — which apparently means something to him.
But overwhelmingly, “Thank You” is messy, noisy glitch-rap fun. Consider “I Don’t Care,” one of the top tracks. It holds a down-tempo pace and finds Mike D weighing the balance of responsibilities and their emotional returns: “We all have a role / I didn’t see mine,” he sings. “Start with a goal get lost in the deadline.” The track excels thanks to wonderful Mini Korg synth work from Hubert Blanc-Fracard, formerly one half of the French music duo Cassius.
Despite a dash of low lights, “Thank You” is refreshingly inventive. That in itself is an accomplishment. To have the aim and drive to create something this new and far afield deserves applause. He’s reaching beyond the low rung recreations of Beastie Boy flavor he could have easily leaned into. But that’s easy and accessible and where’s the fun in that?
Credit is due here for exploration and commitment. He’s Mike D and he gets respect.
___
“Thank You,” by Mike D 5D
Three stars out of five
On repeat: “I Don’t Care”
Skip it: “Crypto”
For fans of: A distressed “Paul’s Boutique”

articles.title: Deportees who refused to exit a US flight in Liberia are sent to Equatorial Guinea
articles.body:
Deportees who refused to exit a US flight in Liberia are sent to Equatorial Guinea
DAKAR, Senegal (AP) — Six people who were deported by the United States to Liberia last week resisted getting off the plane and instead were sent to Equatorial Guinea, another African nation that signed a third-country deportation agreement with the Trump administration, a person on the plane and a lawyer in contact with the six said Monday.
Under a series of often secret agreements, the Trump administration has deported thousands of people to two dozen countries that aren’t their own as it pushes ahead with its immigration crackdown, advocates say. Immigration lawyers say the practice is being used as a legal loophole to indirectly return some asylum seekers to countries they fled.
The group who refused to get off the plane in Liberia on Thursday include four Cuban men, a Brazilian man and a Cameroonian woman, the person and lawyer said.
A Honduran deportee aboard the flight said the group refused to disembark, saying Liberia was “not their country” and that they would face danger there. They were then separated from the others, he said. He spoke on condition of anonymity out of fear of reprisals.
He said the other passengers got off in Liberia because they feared officers would force them.
Meredyth Yoon, litigation director for Asian Americans Advancing Justice-Atlanta, said the deportees who resisted leaving the plane in Liberia were told they would be returned to the United States but instead were flown to Malabo city in Equatorial Guinea.
“It was a really heartbreaking and chaotic scene when they arrived in Malabo on Thursday,” Yoon said.
Some arrived in chains and in extreme distress, she said, including the Cameroonian woman and one of the Cuban men, who Yoon said has a large abdominal growth and uses a colostomy bag that must be drained regularly.
There is no medical staff at the hotel in Equatorial Guinea where the six are being held, alongside around 40 other deported migrants, she added.
Conditions at the hotel have worsened in recent months, Yoon said, with food sometimes withheld and guards accused of threatening, beating and choking some of the migrants.
Equatorial Guinea’s government did not immediately respond to a request seeking comment.
Under an opaque $7.5 million deal with the Trump administration, Equatorial Guinea’s all-powerful president, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, has turned the hotel owned by his family into a prison for asylum seekers deported from the U.S.

articles.title: Two UN peacekeepers killed in ambush while on patrol in South Sudan, seven others injured
articles.body:
Two UN peacekeepers were killed in an ambush while on a patrol in South Sudan's Jonglei state on Monday, the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) said in a statement.
Seven others were injured when unidentified armed men attacked the patrol as it traveled to Pajut, the UN mission added.
The wounded included three peacekeepers, two South Sudan National Police Service personnel and two civilian staff.
UNMISS said it deployed a Quick Reaction Force to secure the area and support the emergency response.
"Such deadly violence targeting UNMISS personnel who are serving to support peace in South Sudan is unacceptable," Anita Kiki Gbeho, the head of UNMISS, said.
UN mission in South Sudan calls for investigation into attack
The mission called for a prompt investigation and said attacks on UN peacekeepers may constitute war crimes under international law.
Attacks on UN personnel are rare but not unprecedented in South Sudan, where UNMISS patrols operate in volatile areas affected by intercommunal fighting, armed youth mobilizations and clashes involving government forces.

Mexico president says Sinaloa governor's brief return to office was 'not appropriate'
MEXICO CITY, Aug 24 - Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Monday it was "not appropriate" for Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha to return to his post after accusations of drug trafficking by the United States.
Rocha, 77, a member of the ruling Morena party, dramatically returned to office on Friday but backtracked on Saturday following sharp criticism from Sheinbaum and other members of Morena.
"I had no prior knowledge that he wanted to return," Sheinbaum said at her daily morning press conference on Monday, adding that the Sinaloa state congress is expected to appoint an interim governor.
In April, U.S. prosecutors charged Rocha with conspiring with the Sinaloa Cartel to traffic drugs into the United States in exchange for bribes and political support.
Rocha has denied the charges, calling them a politically motivated attack.
Sheinbaum previously questioned the U.S. evidence against Rocha, but his brief return to office exposed tensions within the ruling party over the high-profile cartel allegations. REUTERS

articles.title: 'Hindu baiter': CM Himanta slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti row
articles.body:
Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti comment. Photo credit: ANI
NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Monday joined the escalating political row over Rahul Gandhi’s remarks on the Manusmriti, accusing the Congress leader of using women’s rights as a 'smokescreen' to target Hinduism and challenging him to support a Uniform Civil Code (UCC).Sarma, in a post on X, said, “Rahul Gandhi is NO champion of women’s rights. He is simply a Hindu baiter, using the cause of women’s empowerment as a convenient smokescreen to target and discredit Hindu Dharma.”The Assam chief minister’s remarks came after Gandhi, during an interaction with girl students in Pune on Saturday, criticised what he called a “Manusmriti mindset” and urged women to “smash patriarchy”.Sarma questioned Gandhi’s position by asking, “Consider this: how many times has he spoken with the same outrage against patriarchal and medieval practices that persist under Sharia? NEVER.”He further argued that Manusmriti and Sharia should not be treated as equivalent sources of authority, writing, “While Sharia is foundational to Islamic jurisprudence, Manusmriti has no comparable scriptural authority in Hindu Dharma. It is not even a universally binding code for Hindus.”
Sarma then directly challenged the Congress leader over the issue of a common civil law. “So here is a simple challenge to Rahul Gandhi: If women’s equality truly comes before politics, will he unequivocally support a Uniform Civil Code that guarantees equal rights irrespective of religion?” he said.
Sarma also alleged that Congress had a record of compromising on women’s rights, referring to the Shah Bano case and the Triple Talaq legislation. He further claimed that Gandhi had ensured that no woman was included in the Karnataka state Cabinet.
The remarks came after the LoP’s interaction with students, where he said women should not be defined solely through their relationships with men.Rahul said women belong to themselves and not to their fathers, husbands or sons, while describing as shameful the Manusmriti’s prescription that women remain under the authority of male relatives at different stages of their lives.Referring to a verse from the ancient text, Gandhi said, “These words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken.”The controversy has since widened, with Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis among other prominent BJP faces criticised Rahul’s remarks.CM Adityanath earlier questioned Gandhi’s role as Leader of Opposition and said, “Whether you accept the Manusmriti or not is your choice, but do not acquaint people with wrong facts.”

articles.title: Saudi vessel attacked in Red Sea, national shipping company confirms following Houthi claims
articles.body:
The Saudi Amzan ship was attacked in the Red Sea on Monday, Saudi Arabia's national shipping company Bahri confirmed in a statement, noting that all crew members were safe and no injuries had been reported.
The confirmation comes following claims by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis earlier on Monday that they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia’s port city of Yanbu, in comments by the group’s military spokesperson Yahya Saree in a televised speech.
Earlier in the day, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile 63 nautical miles west of Yanbu.
The UKMTO said all crew were safe and accounted for with no reported environmental impact.
Yanbu is Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea oil port, where millions of barrels a day are loaded, and has become the main route for Saudi oil skirting the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blockaded.
Red Sea blockade declared by Houthis against Saudi ships
Shipping from Yanbu has itself faced disruption since the Houthis declared a blockade on Saudi-linked vessels in the Red Sea last month.
The Houthis have carried out attacks on Saudi oil facilities and shipping in the Red Sea in recent weeks, and they claimed to have targeted Saudi oil giant Aramco facilities in Yanbu in July.

Indonesia’s Ministry of Forestry and Vantara, founded by Anant Ambani, Executive Director of Reliance Industries Limited, have announced a partnership focused on strengthening wildlife health infrastructure, veterinary care and conservation efforts in Indonesia.The programme will include training for elephant caregivers, veterinarians and officials involved in wildlife management, along with 10 veterinary hospitals, or ‘Hospitals on Wheels’ for wild animals across Indonesia. The Way Kambas Elephant Hospital will be upgraded into an Elephant Treatment and Care Centre with equipment and technology.
The upgraded facility is expected to support 62 Sumatran elephants under human care and nearly 100 wild Sumatran elephants in the surrounding landscape, according to the announcement.The programme is part of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Indonesian government and Vantara covering wildlife health, animal welfare and conservation. The cooperation also includes conservation breeding, rehabilitation, rewilding, in situ and ex situ conservation, and capacity building.
Vantara will provide veterinary expertise, technical support, infrastructure assistance and training in programmes led by Indonesian authorities, working with national institutions and Fauna Land.
Indonesia’s Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said the cooperation would strengthen the country’s ability to care for wildlife while ensuring that the programmes remain under Indonesian authorities.“Wildlife conservation is ultimately our responsibility, and we must ensure that Indonesia has the facilities, expertise and resources to care for our wildlife wherever they need us. Through this partnership, we are strengthening our own wildlife health and conservation infrastructure, with Vantara supporting us with its experience, expertise and resources,” Antoni said.Vantara CEO Vivaan Karani said the organisation would share its experience in wildlife health, veterinary care, animal husbandry and conservation while also learning from Indonesia’s conservation work.
“Indonesia is home to some of the world's most extraordinary biodiversity, and it is a privilege for Vantara to support the country in protecting this heritage for future generations,” Karani said. “Most importantly, we want this partnership to deliver something practical and lasting for wildlife.”Faunaland CEO Danny Gunalen said the partnership could help strengthen local capacity and wildlife infrastructure.“Indonesia is blessed with extraordinary wildlife and biodiversity, and protecting this natural heritage is a responsibility we all share,
” Gunalen said. “We hope this partnership will build local capacity, strengthen the infrastructure available to wildlife and, most importantly, make a real and lasting difference to the animals and the people dedicated to protecting them.”The cooperation will follow Indonesia’s national conservation priorities and applicable laws and policies, with its success ultimately measured by how effectively the new support reaches animals in need and translates into stronger, lasting protection for endangered species across the country.

articles.title: Istanbul court announces verdict in opposition mayors’ case
articles.body:
An Istanbul court on Aug. 24 delivered its verdict in the trial of seven opposition mayors and municipal officials, acquitting businessman Aziz İhsan Aktaş, who had been referred to as the alleged ringleader of a criminal organization, of charges of establishing an organization to manipulate tenders.
The case was brought over allegations that Aktaş bribed mayors and municipal officials to orchestrate public tenders. The court ruled that Aktaş was acquitted of the charges of “establishing a criminal organization.” However, he was sentenced to two years in prison for rigging public tenders and was also banned from participating in public tenders for two years.
The court was issuing separate verdicts for each defendant over their alleged roles in more than 60 acts involving bid-rigging, while the reading of the full verdict was expected to continue until the evening.
Avcılar Mayor Utku Caner Çaykara was acquitted of two charges.
Former Esenyurt Mayor Ahmet Özer was sentenced to eight months and 10 days in prison for “abuse of office through negligence.” Özer was also banned from serving as civil servant.
Beşiktaş Mayor Rıza Akpolat, who was accused of involvement in 52 acts, has so far been acquitted of 18 of them. Akpolat was sentenced to two years and eight months in prison for rigging public tenders and an additional three years for accepting bribes. The reading of the verdicts concerning Akpolat is still ongoing.
The first hearing of the trial was held on Jan. 27, after the indictment was accepted by the court. During the roughly six-month period between the first hearing and July 29, the court held 59 hearings.
The number of defendants in pretrial detention, which stood at 33 when the trial began, has fallen to five following a series of release rulings. A total of 28 defendants, including Adana Mayor Zeydan Karalar,
Adana’s Ceyhan Mayor Kadir Aydar and Istanbul’s Avcılar Mayor Çaykara, Istanbul’s Esenyurt former Mayor Özer, was released pending trial.
However, Istanbul’s Beşiktaş Mayor Akpolat and Adana’s Seyhan Mayor Oya Tekin were jailed pending trial.

Arvind Kejriwal will address a town hall on E20 petrol policy in Goa. Photo credit: ANI
NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Arvind Kejriwal will address a town hall on E20 petrol policy during his two-day visit to Goa beginning Monday.Kejriwal landed at Dabolim Airport in south Goa on Sunday, where he was received by local party leaders.AAP sources said Kejriwal would address a press conference on Monday in Panaji and a town hall a day later on E20 petrol policy.The AAP, which has two MLAs in the 40-member Goa assembly, has announced a campaign against the "forced implementation" of E20 (ethanol-blended) fuel in the coastal state, which will go to polls in 2027.Earlier this month, Kejriwal had demanded the government give the option to choose between pure petrol and E20 at fuel pumps.The Centre introduced E20, a blend of 20 per cent ethanol and 80 per cent petrol, as part of efforts to reduce vehicular emissions and cut dependence on crude oil imports. After a phased rollout, E20 became the only petrol variant available at fuel pumps across the country from April 2026.
The move has triggered concerns among some vehicle owners, with motorists reporting reduced engine performance and apprehensions about damage to fuel lines and other components.
Owners of older vehicles, many of which may not have been designed for high ethanol blends, have been seeking availability of lower blends such as E10.Industry executives had sought to allay concerns over the use of E20 petrol, saying the fuel has undergone rigorous scientific testing, is safe for both new and older vehicles, and is critical for reducing India's dependence on imported crude oil.

articles.title: Two arrested over murder of boxing star
articles.body:
Two arrested over murder of boxing star
Police in South Africa’s Eastern Cape have arrested two men in connection with the murder of former world boxing champion Zolani Tete, who was fatally shot in Mdantsane on Friday.
The two persons of interest, aged 30 and 22, were arrested in Ku Gompo on Saturday following a swift, intelligence-driven operation involving multiple law enforcement units, police said.
Eastern Cape police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana said the suspects were in custody and were being questioned in connection with Tete’s murder and the attempted murder of a 27-year-old woman who was wounded in the attack.
“Due to the sensitive nature of the ongoing investigation, the SAPS is unable to disclose further details regarding the motive or the circumstances surrounding the arrests at this time,” Gantana said. “Investigators are following up on several leads, and more arrests are imminent.”
Tete, 38, was killed outside his home in Mdantsane on Friday evening as he sat in his car waiting for the gate to open. Police said the shooting happened at about 6:30pm. Two armed men wearing balaclavas reportedly got out of another vehicle and opened fire on Tete and the woman travelling with him.
“In an attempt to escape the hail of bullets, the deceased drove his vehicle into the yard. He unfortunately succumbed to his injuries and was declared deceased on the scene,” Gantana said.
The woman sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was taken to a nearby hospital, where she remains. On Saturday, police confirmed Tete’s identity after notifying his next of kin.
Tete was one of South Africa’s most successful boxers, winning world titles in two weight divisions. He also holds a Guinness World Record for the fastest knockout in a world title fight.
On November 18, 2017, he stopped Siboniso Gonya in 11 seconds at the SSE Arena in Belfast. Tete won the International Boxing Federation junior bantamweight title in Kobe, Japan, in July 2014 after stopping Teiru Kinoshita. He later held the World Boxing Organisation bantamweight title from 2017 until losing it to John Riel Casimero in Birmingham in November 2019. He had 34 professional fights, winning 29, including 22 by knockout. Tete grew up in Mdantsane, started boxing at the age of 8 and was trained by former world champion Vuyani Bungu.
He had not fought since July 2022, when he tested positive for the banned steroid stanozolol following his victory over Jason Cunningham at Wembley. The result was overturned to a no contest and Tete was handed a four-year ban, which ended on July 29 this year. Tete maintained that he had never knowingly taken the substance. In an interview with boxing magazine The Ring in January, he said he planned to return to the ring this year.

articles.title: Amnesty urges rescue of worshippers abducted in Nigeria mosque attack
articles.body:
Kabir Adeniyi
24 August 2026•Update: 24 August 2026
 Amnesty International has urged Nigerian authorities to urgently secure the release of worshippers abducted during Friday prayers at a mosque in Niger State, warning of the growing threat posed by mass abductions across the country’s north.
The rights group made the call after terrorists attacked the Kpenya Mosque in Dekara District of Borgu Local Government Area on Aug. 21, abducting an unspecified number of worshippers.
Amnesty described the incident as particularly alarming because the victims were abducted while observing Friday prayers, adding that more than 80 people may have been taken during the attack.
“The Nigerian authorities must act urgently to ensure the safe rescue of the abducted worshippers,” the organization said in a statement Monday.
It also called on the government to address the broader wave of mass abductions targeting rural communities across northern Nigeria.
Amnesty said at least 1,100 people were abducted between January and April 2026, while noting that available figures vary and may significantly underestimate the actual scale of the problem.
The organization warned that victims of previous mass abductions had reported severe abuses, including torture, starvation, sexual violence and amputation.
The Niger State government confirmed the attack and said terrorists stormed the mosque while worshippers were observing Juma’at prayers.
State Commissioner for Information and Orientation Obed Nana said a joint security operation had been deployed to track the attackers and facilitate the rescue of the abducted worshippers.
“A joint security operation has been deployed to assess the situation, track the attackers, and facilitate the rescue of the abducted worshippers,” Nana told Anadolu.
The government declined to disclose further operational details, saying doing so could compromise ongoing rescue efforts, while urging residents to avoid spreading unverified figures.
The Kpenya attack occurred barely a week after an attack on worshippers in the Ungushi community in Sokoto State, where gunmen killed at least 32 people during Friday prayers, including the mosque’s imam.
Anadolu previously reported the Aug. 18 attack in Ungushi, highlighting growing insecurity affecting communities in northwestern Nigeria.
The latest incident adds to a series of attacks reported around the Borgu-Kainji corridor, an area where authorities and security analysts have raised concerns about armed groups operating around Kainji Lake National Park.

articles.title: 'We will die rather than be drafted': extremist Haredi protesters block Highway 4 over arrest of draft evader
articles.body:
Ultra-Orthodox protesters from the extremist Jerusalem Faction are blocking Highway 4 near Bnei Brak in central Israel to protest the arrest of a draft evader who failed to report for IDF service. The demonstrators blocked northbound traffic from the Aluf Sadeh Interchange and southbound traffic from the Em HaMoshavot Interchange on Monday afternoon.
The protesters were heard shouting: "We will die rather than be drafted."
As early as 3 p.m., police urged drivers to avoid the area. Authorities also said the protest was expected to cause traffic congestion and road closures along Jabotinsky Road in Bnei Brak.
The protesters gathered following the arrest of draft evader Yisrael Guhafi, a yeshiva student whom the Am Kadosh organization - an active response group and alert network run by the Jerusalem Faction -  claimed had been “abducted to military prison.” 
He had switched yeshivas in recent days and, while traveling to the new institution, was detained over what was described as a “problem with his Rav-Kav” public transportation card. After his identity was established, he was handed over to the Military Police.
